summary: Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied under Minoru Hara and Katsuhiko Kamimura, earning an MA from the University of Tokyo and a PhD from the University of Groningen. She became an Associate Professor at Kyoto University around 2004.

Yukteshwar Kumar is a sinologist who studied at Visva-Bharati University, Jawaharlal Nehru University under Tan Chung, and Peking University. He has held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, the University of Delhi, and the University of Bath around 2012.

Yulian Zeng works in Buddhist studies. Zeng studied under Hsing Yun and earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University from around 2007 to 2010 under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin.
Yumi Katayama is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who completed PhD studies at Hiroshima University by 2007 under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo.

Yumiko Ishihama specializes in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University from 1980 to 1989, later holding positions at Toyo Bunko around 1985–1986 and Waseda University around 1997.

Yumiko Nakanishi is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD in 2000 at the University of California, Berkeley, where Lewis Lancaster served on her committee.

Yun Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University around 2003–2006. Around 2006, Ji became an assistant professor at Buddhist College of Singapore.

Yun-hua Jan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who studied under Yun-shan Tan from around 1955 to 1960. He was a Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and Professor at McMaster University (~1967–1989).

Yun-shan Tan was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology educated at Hunan Normal University and several academies under Lan-Chi Chen, Ziyuan Long, Taixu, and Kshitimohan Sen. He taught at Lida Academy and Visva-Bharati University (~1937–1968).
Yungfen Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and doctoral supervisor Chun-fang Yu, receiving her PhD in 2011.
Yusen Kashiwahara was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University from around 1937 to 1940 and served as a professor there from around 1968 to 1980.

Yusho Miyasaka was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1944–1947). He served as an assistant professor at Koyasan University (~1957–1974), worked at Shuchiin University (~1974–1990), and was named Professor Emeritus at Nagoya University in 1976.

Yusho Wakahara is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Eshō Mikogami. Wakahara served as a lecturer at Hanazono University and as an assistant professor at Ryukoku University from around 1989 to 2017.
Yutai Ikeda was a scholar of Buddhist studies who held posts at Otani University and Doho University, serving as Emeritus Professor at Doho University around 2005.

Yutaka Hirata was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Kyushu University (~1950–1954), held a post at Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995), and was Professor Emeritus at Kyushu University (~1995–2013).

Yutaka Iwamoto was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936) under Toru Haneda and Hidenaka Tanaka, among others. He held posts at Kyoto Tachibana University (~1968–1971) and Soka University (~1974–1980).
Yutaka Kawasaki is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seio Okuda and held a post at the University of Tokyo.

Yutaka Ochihara was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and under scholars including Atsuuji Ashikaga and Louis Renou. He taught at Kyoto University (1957–1986) and the Collège de France (1985).

Yutaka Takagi is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1970 to 1980.

Yutaka Yoshida is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Hitotsubashi University, and held posts at Hitotsubashi University and Kyoto University (~2006–2020).
